newsitem.title: UK: NWE GAS OIL STABLE, DIESEL ARB FROM MED ON HORIZON.
newsitem.headline: NWE GAS OIL STABLE, DIESEL ARB FROM MED ON HORIZON.

text.p: European gas oil differentials were notionally steady in very thin trade affected by work on IPE expiry arrangements and a holiday lull, traders said.
September IPE settled 75 cents easier at $170.00 a tonne. October finished 75 cents down at $172.00 in listless trade.

A trading house was heard offering Italian low sulphur diesel at low numbers around September IPE +$1.50 in the Med, arousing speculation it sought to depress values in southern Europe to facilitate an arbitrage to the north.
But traders said that to become workable, the NWE low sulphur diesel differential would have to widen at least another $1 to around September IPE +$6 or +$7.
Wednesday's notional value remained at around $4/$5.

Volumes were thin, affected by holidays and slack heating oil demand. Some traders spent time involved in a debate on a proposed IPE alteration to the physical delivery rules requiring longs to give provide written confirmation that their product is in tank in ARA.
On the barge market, second half August was screen flat to a 50 cent discount. Low sulphur diesel was talked around September +$3.25/$4.50 although one trade was rumoured around $1 lower.
